sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Lightweight Ad-Monetized Mobile Games

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (Articles L.561-1 et seq. and L.561-2 et seq.), Ordonnance n° 2020-306 du 25 mars 2020 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment des capitaux et le financement du terrorisme, and Décret establishing the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of identity of Ultimate Beneficial Owner (passport or national ID card)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Notarization and Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic (French and EU) sanctions and adverse media screening protocols

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: infogreffe.fr (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirements for French language and Latin script; company names must be in French or accompanied by French translation if in another language
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Reserved words for public services (banque, assurance, état, etc.), offensive or misleading terms, names infringing intellectual property
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation valid for 1 month; extendable by 1 month. Upon rejection or modification, administrative appeal to the Tribunal de Commerce or modification request via guichet-entreprises.fr

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for most sectors including gaming; must designate a registered office address in France for RCS purposes, virtual or physical acceptable if compliant with legal requirements
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (under 10%) for standard incorporation; higher during subsequent regulatory inspections or tax compliance checks

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company incorporation and RCS filing fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee of approximately 250 EUR plus legal drafting

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification, due diligence, and AML/CFT screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for international due diligence services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization and apostille for foreign UBO documents
Registered office setup and compliance documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for virtual or physical office compliance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 governing Societe a Responsabilite Limitee; Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general provisions); implementing regulations R.223-1 et seq.; formalities administered through the INPI Guichet Unique under Decret n° 2023-253.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Societes (RCS) maintained by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; incorporation dossiers are submitted electronically via the INPI Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts d'une SARL (articles of association); Demande d'immatriculation au RCS (Form M0); Acte de nomination du Gerant; Attestation de depot des fonds.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for a SARL; the articles may fix capital at any amount (e.g. EUR 1). Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked escrow bank account and at least 20% of each contribution paid up at subscription; the balance must be paid in full within five years. Contributions in kind must be fully paid up on registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the founding shareholders adopt these Articles of Association and approve the share subscriptions made by each member in the amounts and forms set out in the incorporation schedule; such subscriptions are irrevocably undertaken on the terms therein. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office shall be fixed at [address], France, and the legal representative shall complete all filings at the RCS. The shareholders appoint [Gerant Name] as first Manager, with full corporate authority, and authorize the opening of a blocked escrow deposit account and any bank accounts necessary for the Company's formation and operations. Each officer accepts their appointment and shall attend to statutory publication, registration, and commissioning of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft statutory documents and legal announcement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional) or legal counsel; no direct filing with registry until step 4
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the signed form of SARL Articles (Statuts), the appointment deed of the first Manager (Gerant), and the draft legal notice for announcement in an approved Journal d'Annonces Legales. Verify shareholder identity and capital subscription schedules.
required_dossiers: Proof of address for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry notes deficiencies, amend the Statuts by unanimous consent or by the proposed shareholders' vote and re-draft the announcement accordingly before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open blocked escrow account and deposit capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution (bank) or Caisse des Depots et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital deposit account in the Company's future name. Collect cash contributions; for contributions in kind, obtain the statutory report of the commissaire aux apports if required. The bank issues the attestation de depot des fonds evidencing block release condition until RCS registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries beneficial ownership or source of funds, provide KYC documents, corporate precedents, and lawful source evidence; re-deposit or cure discrepancies within the bank's designated period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sign statuts and publish legal notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders and manager; legal announcement published by an approved Journal d'Annonces Legales (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the constitutive shareholders' meeting; execute the Statuts and the manager appointment deed; instruct the JAL to publish the legal notice. All signatories may execute by private signature unless notarization is voluntarily chosen or required by asset contribution.
required_dossiers: Beneficial owners declaration (Declaration des beneficiaires effectifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is refused or inaccurate, correct the announcement with the JAL and obtain a rectified attestation; no rejection by RCS will occur if corrected before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit incorporation dossier through Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites d'entreprise), which transmits to the RCS/Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the INPI Guichet Unique portal and complete Form M0, attaching all required documents. Make the online payment of registry fees (frais de greffe). Monitor the dossier until receipt of the RCS immatriculation request reference.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of shareholders and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If INPI/RCS issues a regularization notice, cure missing documents by uploading the requested item in the prescribed period (usually 15 days); if rejection becomes final, refile with corrected documents and pay any new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Kbis extract and effect post-registration formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS); DGFiP for tax registration; URSSAF for social registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, obtain the Kbis extract (official company registration certificate), confirm the SIREN/SIRET and APE/NAF code, activate tax and social security accounts, and release the blocked capital deposit with the bank by presenting the Kbis.
required_dossiers: Manager's identity and residency proof for opening bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains errors or is delayed, request rectification against the Greffe by presenting contradictory documents; administrative delay beyond statutory limit may be escalated via a formal notice to the registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to ISIC 5820 digital publishing; no industrial development board authorization is required for an SARL engaged in hyper-casual game publishing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or manufacturing operating permit required; only the RCS Kbis and standard sectoral compliance (gaming age-rating where applicable) apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de la Transition Ecologique / DREAL (Direction Regionale de l'Environnement, de l'Amenagement et du Logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - activity is not a regulated ICPE installation; no EIA is required for a software publishing office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to industrial wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste; general office waste must be disposed under municipal contracts and small-volume electronic waste under WEEE regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: As a private office without public access, no ERP fire clearance or special civil defense permit is required; employer must nevertheless comply with Code du travail safety obligations (fire extinguisher checks, electrical inspections, training) and ensure the leased premises have valid fire safety arrangements under Articles R.4214-1 and R.4227-1.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) via impots.gouv.fr; customs and export VAT supervision: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) via douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities incorporating or establishing a French SARL must file legal and tax registration through the 'Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises' (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) to obtain SIREN/SIRET and the KBis company extract. The DGFIP then allocates the French intra-community VAT number (FR + 2-digit checksum + 9-digit SIREN). Non-established foreign taxable persons making supplies in France must use the DGFIP non-resident registration procedure (Form 12103/Cerfa n° 12103*7) and may be required to appoint a tax representative if they have no EU establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box regime. A SARL is subject by default to entity-level corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) under CGI Article 206; a qualifying 'family SARL' may elect pass-through individual income tax under CGI Article 239. Applicable group elections include 'intégration fiscale' (tax consolidation) for French companies operating through a 95%+ French subsidiary chain. Hybrid mismatch outcomes must be reported on the statutory hybrid declaration and are subject to ATAD disallowance rules rather than elective treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA — taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 34,400 for predominantly service activities (including digital and distance services); EUR 85,000 for goods sales under CGI Article 293 B — annual turnover thresholds for the 'franchise en base de TVA'.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for B2B supplies on a phased basis: from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and 1 September 2027 for SMEs, receivable through certified Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDP) using Factur-X, UBL, or CII formats; invoice data is transmitted via PDP APIs to DGFIP for e-reporting. France does not currently impose transaction-level fiscal stamping or pre-clearance continuous controls, but e-reporting of B2B and B2C transaction data is required, and public-sector invoices already use the Chorus Pro portal. Non-EU suppliers using digital platforms may have compliance obligations under the OSS/IOSS schemes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For physical exports of goods outside the EU, the supply is zero-rated under CGI Article 262(I) if title and risk pass to the non-resident buyer and the goods are physically shipped outside the EU within the prescribed evidentiary period (usually 90 days from supply). For services, hyper-casual mobile game advertising monetization is generally assessed under the B2B place-of-supply rule based on the customer's establishment; non-EU B2B customers keep the service outside French VAT, while EU B2C digital services may trigger the OSS scheme. The taxable person must retain commercial, transport, and banking proof of the actual cross-border movement or the foreign customer's establishment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Déclaration d'exportation) filed electronically via DELTA/GUN, bearing an export declaration number
Bill of lading, air waybill, or CMR road consignment note indicating France/European Community as departure origin and non-EU destination
Inward remittance certificate or bank SWIFT/transfer confirmation evidencing collection of export proceeds from the foreign buyer
Commercial invoice, packing list, and sales contract
Proof of physical exit from EU customs territory (exit summary statement, export accompaniment document/ELBA, or destination customs record)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFIP rigorously examines export evidence; if zero-rating is disallowed, the tax administration reassesses output VAT with intérêt de retard (0.20% per month), a 10% late-payment inclusion, a 40% deliberate-omission penalty (manquement délibéré), or an 80% penalty for fraudulent maneuvering/abus de droit. Criminal prosecution under CGI Article 1741 may include imprisonment and fines of up to EUR 500,000 or 500% of evaded tax. Customs authorities may impose confiscation and additional monetary penalties under the French Customs Code where false export declarations are used, with a three-year assessment limitation extended to ten years for tax fraud, and potential joint and several liability of the legal representative.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (French central bank and balance-of-payments statistical authority), acting jointly with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) under the Code Monétaire et Financier and the Haut Conseil de Stabilité Financière.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is freely convertible in both current and capital accounts under EU directives 88/361/EEC and Articles 63-65 TFEU; the French FX-control regime imposes no licensing or exchange-control approval on trade, profit remittance, or debt service. Capital and current movements are freely executed through an authorised resident bank, but must satisfy financial information reporting thresholds. In practice, profit repatriation by a French SARL requires annual accounts approval, a CEO/manager remittance resolution, tax residency and beneficial ownership certification for treaty relief, and a positive solvency test under French corporate law; the standard French dividend tax of 30% (12.8% income tax plus 17.2% social levies) applies absent EU parent-subsidiary or treaty reduction. No French FX authorisation is required for dividend remittance; the only hurdle is compliance with bank documentary and anti-money-laundering expectations. Non-resident shareholders may hold 100% of the SARL, and currency conversion at the time of market payment is carried out by the receiving/remitting bank at freely negotiated market rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio for export or commercial proceeds in France. Exporters are not required to convert foreign currency receipts into euro, nor are they obliged to repatriate them into France within a specified number of days, provided the funds are held in an account in a compliant financial institution. However, French economic statistics require all cross-border settlements exceeding EUR 50,000 (or cash transactions above EUR 10,000) to be reported by the resident intermediary bank to Banque de France using standard balance-of-payments transaction codes. For a hyper-casual gaming publisher, export proceeds consist of ad-network payouts and digital goods sales; the company must preserve traffic, sales and transaction-level settlement reports by country of residence of the payer, alongside VAT evidence, to substantiate export treatment and ensure accurate purpose-code classification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte de Consignation) and Multi-Currency Operational Treasury Account (EUR, USD, GBP) with SWIFT/FileAct connectivity
Operational Corporate Account with Cross-Border Payment Factory and FX Forward Line
Operational Account with Cash-Sweeping and Trade Service Escrow Sub-Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Core treasury viability is Moderate-to-High for operational disbursements: a French-licensed or EU-passported Electronic Money Institution (EMI) under PSD2 may hold payment accounts, execute SEPA/SWIFT payment initiation, and deliver multi-currency FX conversion. Legal constraints: an EMI is not a credit institution and cannot provide an escrow guarantee, negotiate commercial letters of credit, or offer deposit-like lending services without an additional credit-institution licence; the French banking monopoly under Articles L511-1 et seq. of the Code Monétaire et Financier prevents non-banks from taking deposits from the public. Accordingly, EMIs such as Qonto, Shine, N26 and Lydia are best deployed as operational rails for inbound ad-network payouts and outbound traffic-acquisition settlements, whereas a full-service tier-1 bank should remain the sole custodian of subscribed capital and statutory escrow funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML legislation (Code Monétaire et Financier, Articles L561-2 to L561-27) permits fully remote onboarding through certified digital identity verification, including video conference and liveness checks, in line with ACPR guidance. However, tier-1 banks universally require a substantive compliance interview with the legal representative/managing director (gérant) and identification of each beneficial owner holding more than 25% of capital. Physical presence is no longer strictly mandatory if the bank offers video KYC; if the managing director is a non-resident natural person, the bank will typically request an apostilled passport, a proof of residence, and either a physical interview at a French branch or a remote interview with a qualified executive, plus a notarised copy of the deed of appointment. Foreign corporate beneficial owners additionally need certified constitutional documents and a bank reference from a reputable source jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting flag: newly incorporated SARL with no audited financials and expected revenue entirely from rapid high-frequency ad-tech payouts originating from foreign digital aggregator networks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal existence pack: certificates of incorporation, articles of association, UBO declaration filed under Article L561-46, non-resident shareholder register, proof of tax registration (Kbis and SIREN/SIRET), and an extract of the legal representative's appointment. Operational substance pack: signed agreements with AdMob and AppLovin, App Store and Google Play developer console screenshots showing the registered company, six months of projected revenue dashboards, AppsFlyer or similar attribution reports, a documented description of the real-time auction model, and a written internal AML/transaction-monitoring policy demonstrating segregation of player funds from corporate cash.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting flag: cross-border capital injection from an offshore non-resident shareholder into the SARL's bank account, creating source-of-funds uncertainty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder source-of-wealth file: bank reference letters from the remitting financial institution, notarised or apostilled corporate resolutions authorising the capital transfer, personal or corporate audited financial statements, a legal source-of-funds declaration, tax residence certificates, and evidence that the capital will be used for the disclosed purpose of acquiring studio development and traffic-acquisition contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting flag: tranched outbound disbursements to many unverified media-buying vendors for user acquisition, with payment destinations in high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Procurement and campaign file: executed media-buying agreements or insertion orders with Supply-Side Platforms, itemised vendor invoices including campaign IDs, live campaign reports showing impressions/installs and eCPA, auction and DSP account ownership statements, attestation of no cash transaction settlement, and a reconciliation schedule demonstrating that outgoing disbursements correspond to actual advertising consumption and contractual fee milestones.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting flag: gaming publisher operating without a statutory licence, causing uncertainty as to regulatory posture and potential unlicensed gambling or consumer-protection exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance attestation file: an external legal opinion confirming the hyper-casual game is not a 'jeu d'argent' under Article L561-1 of the French Gaming Code, published privacy policy and GDPR compliance documentation, age-rating certificates (IARC / PEGI), payout rules showing no real-money exchange or cash-out mechanics, and evidence of the ad-supported freemium model with no pay-to-win circulation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Subscribed capital and shareholder loans must arrive by SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA CT for euro transfers initiated by a French/EU bank) to the SARL's opening account held with a French licensed bank. The instructing bank must include the full business name of the company, the purpose of the transaction, and the Banque de France balance-of-payments investment code 'A07' for direct investment abroad into France, with a narrative reference such as 'Apport en capital souscrit - création de la SARL FR_SARL' whenever the recipient is a French company. Where the subscriber is an EU parent, the transfer may use payout code 'S604' or the equivalent statutory reporting code for a parent-subsidiary contribution. The receiving bank will require three complete supporting records: (i) the signed board/shareholders' resolution approving the capital increase, (ii) a banker's confirmation of the account number and the capital-escrow nature of the account, and (iii) a certificate of beneficial ownership confirming the immediate and ultimate holding chain. No prior French administrative approval is needed; the obligation is a post-event statistical declaration by the bank to Banque de France for any capital operation exceeding EUR 50,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing rails for a hyper-casual game company follow the nature of the counterparty. For European suppliers and sub-publishers, SEPA Credit Transfers are standard. For non-EEA service providers in digital advertising, cloud analytics, or SDK licensing, settlement runs over SWIFT MT103 with the correct IETF/ISO 20022 purpose code (e.g. 'B108' for data-processing and hosting services, 'R001' for licence fees, 'N400' for advertisement and marketing services). Implemented rails: (1) a payment factory through the tier-1 bank aggregating settlement lines with an API/EBICS channel and reconcilement against invoices; (2) SWIFT MT103 for USD/EUR/GBP high-value disbursements; (3) commercial letters of credit are accessible but, for digital services, typically replaced by a guarantee or an escrow account tied to campaign margin deposits; if the company imports physical merchandise or in-game physical loyalty goods exceeding EUR 50,000, a documentary L/C issued against shipping documents is the preferred low-risk instrument. All outbound traffic-acquisition payments must be matched with campaign insertion orders and DSP invoices to maintain an audit trail for the bank's transaction-monitoring obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (change à terme) on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/SGD with maturity aligned to monthly ad-network settlement cycles
FX swaps (casse de report) for temporary conversion of USD ad-tech receipts into euro while preserving USD liquidity for overseas vendor disbursements
Over-the-counter plain-vanilla European FX options (call/put and zero-cost collars) for uncertain ad-revenue streams in USD
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to exotic or restricted convertibility currencies only, with underlying documentation on the ad-network payout exposure
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for longer-term mismatch when the company holds capital injections or licensing receivables in foreign currencies, subject to EMIR clearing and margin thresholds
Multi-currency zero-balance and pooled notional cash-sweeping arrangements to reduce the need for direct FX and allow natural offset of receivables in the same currency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approved financial statements (comptes annuels) with management report and shareholders' meeting approval resolution — deposit at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) via Infogreffe / Registre National des Entreprises (RNE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 December fiscal year-end: shareholders' meeting approving accounts by 30 June; deposit with the registry within one month after approval (effective latest filing date: 31 July). For other fiscal year-ends: approval within 6 months of close, deposit within 1 month of approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to judicial monetary penalties and possible court order under penalty ('astreinte'); repeated non-deposit for two consecutive fiscal years exposes the company to compulsory strike-off from the RCS after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale IS) — Cerfa 2065-SD and required annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end, e-filing is due by the first working day of the fourth month after close (typically 3 May); otherwise, the return is due within 3 months after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a late-filing surcharge of 5% to 10% of the assessed corporate income tax (CGI Art. 1728), plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.4% (CGI Art. 1727), and may lead to official tax assessment after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial-owner information (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs — RBE record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via Infogreffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation is made concurrently with the deposit of the annual accounts; any share-transfer or control change must be declared within 30 days after the relevant event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or updating incorrectly can result in fines of up to EUR 10,000 for natural persons and EUR 50,000 for legal persons, and may trigger restrictions on voting rights or dividend distribution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Appointment of an independent statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) is mandatory if two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years: balance-sheet total > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average permanent workforce > 50. A voluntary auditor may be appointed by the shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général / ANC Regulation No. 2014-03, as amended) for individual statutory accounts; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for consolidated statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The beneficial-owner declaration must be kept accurate in the RBE record. Annually, when depositing approved accounts, the SARL confirms that the information remains unchanged; any shareholding transfer or change in control requires a separate updated declaration within 30 days of the transaction. The annual confirmation accompanies the statutory accounts filing and creates a public record of the current direct or indirect owners.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 160 – USD 540 (approximately EUR 150 – EUR 500 per year) for commercial domiciliation or registered-office agent services in France; actual costs vary by city and service level.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,400 – USD 16,300 (approximately EUR 5,000 – EUR 15,000) for a first-time French-GAAP statutory audit engagement applicable to a hyper-casual mobile game SARL, if audit thresholds are exceeded or an audit is voluntarily appointed.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying intellectual-property income may be taxed at a 10% rate on net income under the French IP regime, subject to nexus and tracing requirements. The French R&D tax credit is generally 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold. Qualifying newly created companies and Young Innovative Enterprises may obtain relief subject to statutory conditions. Gaming revenue, advertising revenue, and software development are not automatically eligible for preferential treatment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD for corporate income tax, filed electronically through the French tax administration portal using EDI-TDFC or the applicable professional online filing service on impots.gouv.fr. Relevant tax computation annexes generally include forms 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD, 2059-A-SD, 2059-B-SD, 2059-C-SD, and the applicable balance-sheet, income-statement, and tax-adjustment schedules in the 2050-2057 series.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; quarterly or installment payments may apply during the fiscal year but do not replace the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the deadline is generally the second business day following 1 May of the following year, subject to the tax administration's published calendar and any permitted electronic-filing tolerance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, fiscal year dates, business activity, tax office, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the French SARL's registered office, SIREN, French tax office, and French permanent-establishment information where ownership or management is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss adjusted for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax credits, depreciation differences, provisions, and other French tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only profits attributable to the French entity or French permanent establishment and reconcile foreign-parent charges using arm's-length documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting result to taxable result, including permanent additions, deductions, and temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify non-deductible intra-group charges, withholding taxes, provisions, entertainment expenses, fines, and foreign-source items separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss, carried-forward losses, carried-back losses where elected, and losses utilized against current taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only losses legally attributable to the French taxpayer; do not import losses of a foreign parent or sister company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax credits, incentives, deductions, and taxable income computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim R&D, IP, or other incentives only where statutory eligibility, nexus, expenditure tracing, and supporting records are maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of disposals of fixed assets, securities, and other capital items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose disposals involving foreign group entities and apply French participation-exemption or capital-gain rules only where conditions are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exemptions, special tax regimes, and relevant capital-gain classifications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document treaty, EU, participation, restructuring, or IP-regime claims and retain ownership and holding-period evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet, income statement, depreciation, provisions, receivables, payables, and accounting information supporting the tax return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report French statutory accounts and ensure intercompany balances, platform receivables, advertising revenue, royalties, and shareholder accounts reconcile to the ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Corporate income tax installments and balance payment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Four installments may apply based on prior-year corporate income tax, followed by the final balance payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SARL is generally subject to French installment and balance-payment rules; non-resident ownership does not remove the French company's payment obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Late, omitted, or amended returns and supporting explanations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File corrective returns promptly, calculate additional tax and interest, and disclose material transfer-pricing or withholding errors before an audit where possible.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increased in specified circumstances, plus late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month. Tax understatements may attract 40% penalties for deliberate non-compliance or abuse of law and 80% penalties for fraudulent conduct or abusive maneuvers. Criminal tax-fraud sanctions may apply independently.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for distributions by a French company to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. A qualifying EU parent company may obtain exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary regime, generally requiring qualifying legal form, subject-to-tax status, minimum participation, holding-period, and anti-abuse conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility, apply the treaty rate only where French procedural requirements are satisfied, and retain ownership, holding-period, substance, and anti-abuse evidence. Where advance clearance or reduced-rate procedures are required, submit the prescribed French tax forms or treaty documentation through the paying company's tax administration channel. If treaty conditions are uncertain, withhold at the domestic rate and pursue a refund claim using the applicable French form and supporting tax-residence certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to a domestic withholding tax of 25%, subject to treaty reduction or exemption and EU directives where applicable. France generally has no broad domestic withholding tax on ordinary interest paid to non-residents, but exceptions apply, including certain payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions and anti-abuse situations. Treaty interest and royalty rates vary by treaty and commonly range from 0% to 15%; the specific treaty, beneficial-owner status, residence certificate, and limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test provisions must be reviewed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150,000,000 of annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets, or equivalent group-control conditions, generally triggers the French comprehensive transfer-pricing documentation regime, including Local File and Master File requirements. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups meeting the EUR 750,000,000 consolidated-revenue threshold. Below the main threshold, the arm's-length rule still applies and the taxpayer must provide sufficient information on request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a single standalone economic-substance regulation equivalent to certain offshore ESR regimes. Substance is nevertheless relevant under the arm's-length principle, general anti-abuse doctrine, beneficial-ownership analysis, EU anti-abuse rules, interest limitation rules, controlled-foreign-company rules, withholding-tax relief, and the principal-purpose test in treaties. A French SARL should maintain genuine French management, decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises where commercially appropriate, accounting records, bank functions, and documented functions, assets, and risks. A French company that merely receives advertising-platform proceeds and remits them to a foreign group without performing or evidencing substantive functions presents significant recharacterization and treaty-benefit risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing advertising revenue, app-store proceeds, platform receivables, related-party income, or taxable French activities; maintaining false books; fabricating expenses; or deliberately filing materially false corporate tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax reassessment, late-payment interest, penalties generally up to 40% for deliberate conduct and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers, and potential criminal tax-fraud penalties of up to five years' imprisonment and EUR 500,000, with higher sanctions in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may face criminal prosecution, civil liability for losses caused by misconduct, management bans, and personal tax liability in cases of fraudulent or repeated obstruction under French tax law. A corporate veil is not pierced automatically. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be ordered by a court in relevant criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive royalties, management fees, user-acquisition fees, cloud costs, or financing costs to the French SARL; using unsupported commission arrangements; or shifting mobile-game profits to a low-tax affiliate without functional and economic support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustments under the French arm's-length principle, corresponding secondary tax consequences, interest, penalties, withholding-tax exposure, and possible documentation penalties. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation may result in a penalty generally linked to the reassessed amount and subject to statutory minimums and maximums.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability for approving knowingly unsupported arrangements and may face criminal exposure if the structure forms part of fraudulent tax evasion. Personal liability is fact-dependent and is not created solely by an ordinary transfer-pricing adjustment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, service fees, or other French-source amounts to non-residents without determining the applicable domestic rate, treaty conditions, beneficial ownership, or required residence documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid withholding tax against the French payer, late-payment interest, surcharges, possible denial of treaty relief, and penalties for inaccurate or omitted reporting. The payer may remain liable even where the foreign recipient received the gross amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for deliberate or grossly negligent failure to withhold and criminal exposure where withholding-tax fraud is intentional. Personal assessment is not automatic and generally requires statutory conditions or serious misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the French SARL as a conduit with no real functions, employees, decision-making, commercial rationale, or control over assets and risks, solely to obtain treaty benefits, deductions, or access to French banking and payment infrastructure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or domestic exemptions, application of anti-abuse rules, tax reassessment, withholding-tax recovery, interest, penalties, and possible criminal investigation where false documentation or fraudulent intent is involved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed to civil claims, management bans, and criminal sanctions for intentional fraud or false declarations. A shell-company finding alone does not automatically create imprisonment or travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify or update the ultimate beneficial owner, submitting inaccurate ownership information, or concealing nominee arrangements and foreign control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential criminal penalties, registry measures, refusal or suspension of corporate formalities, AML escalation, and enhanced scrutiny by financial institutions and payment providers. Penalties depend on the specific omission and applicable French commercial and AML provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and relevant beneficial owner may face personal criminal and civil exposure for knowingly false or incomplete declarations. Management bans may be ordered in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Layering game-advertising proceeds through related entities, nominee accounts, unexplained payment processors, crypto channels, or fabricated invoices to disguise the origin, ownership, or destination of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering may carry imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of EUR 375,000, with aggravated forms carrying higher imprisonment and fines, including confiscation and asset-freezing measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners, and employees who knowingly participate may face personal criminal prosecution, confiscation, management bans, and court-ordered restrictions. Travel bans may be imposed by judicial order but are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain French statutory accounts, booking platform revenue on a cash basis when accrual accounting is required, omitting intercompany balances, destroying records, or approving false annual accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, accounting penalties, rejection of deductions, civil claims, and criminal sanctions for presentation or publication of false accounts or other applicable corporate offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may incur civil liability for losses, criminal liability for knowingly false accounts, and management disqualification. Personal exposure depends on knowledge, participation, and causation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, extracting funds through disguised shareholder loans, continuing payments while insolvent, or preferring related creditors before insolvency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, director liability for insufficient assets in applicable insolvency proceedings, clawback of suspect-period transactions, fines, management bans, and possible criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be ordered to contribute to company liabilities for management faults, prohibited from managing companies, and prosecuted for misuse of corporate assets or bankruptcy-related offences. Imprisonment is fact-specific and not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to distinguish advertising services, in-app purchases, platform commissions, licensing, and electronically supplied services; misapplying place-of-supply rules; or omitting EU VAT reporting and evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, late-payment interest, penalties, joint-and-several collection exposure in specified cases, and possible criminal proceedings for deliberate VAT fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable where they deliberately organized or participated in VAT fraud or caused an insolvency through serious misconduct. Ordinary classification errors generally produce company-level tax liability rather than automatic personal liability.
